name: SPATS
summary: A dedicated acoustic R&D array deployed in IceCube boreholes measured sound propagation, attenuation and noise in Antarctic ice to test the feasibility of a future acoustic ultra-high-energy neutrino detector.
detection_principle: Piezoelectric transmitters and receivers between several boreholes measure acoustic pulses through ice. The resulting sound speed, attenuation and background measurements determine whether pressure pulses from neutrino showers could be identified by a sparse array.
technologies: Thermo-acoustic particle detection with hydrophones or piezoelectric sensors

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: This record describes the historical dedicated acoustic test programme. The cited papers establish its deployed configuration and measurements, not continuous operation through 2026.

timeline.event: First three strings deployed in IceCube boreholes.
Fourth string extended the array to 500 m depth.

collaboration.name: SPATS Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

key_parameters.name: Completed R&D array
key_parameters.value: Four vertical strings with seven acoustic stages per string

results.summary: Noise and transient-source measurements constrained the feasibility and thresholds of acoustic neutrino detection; no astrophysical neutrino observation by the acoustic system was established.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
